title: Saved mouse visual spectra permit invertible gain changes and do not identify information loss
abstract: We tested what saved mouse visual response spectra can show about information loss. We derived the exact minimum gain condition number for an invertible covariance map and applied it to published aggregate cvPCA spectra from Allen Neuropixels and two-photon data. For the first 30 values, the VISp to VISam change can be reproduced by invertible maps with condition numbers 1.268 and 2.335. Across all pairs of saved unit draws, the central 95 percent ranges were 1.192 to 1.483 and 2.021 to 2.858. These ranges are not mouse confidence intervals. We give a sharp multiplicative eigenvalue error threshold and an exact counterexample: two channels have the same Gaussian output law, but one keeps a 30-bit input attribute and the other loses all of it. The evidence supports a change in variance concentration but does not identify information loss or a circuit mechanism. Limits include truncated covariance surrogates, cvPCA bias, no image alignment and no new animal-level test. Code, licensed aggregate inputs, hashes, proof and numerical checks are included.
